takeaways.label: Strong volume-led quarter, margin noise from pass-throughs
takeaways.text: Revenue grew 28% YoY and 16% QoQ, but consolidated EBITDA margin dipped to ~36% as higher freight and one-off employee arrears masked an improving core gases margin of 39%.

takeaways.label: Durgapur on-site plant is live and de-risked
takeaways.text: The 325 TPD plant commissioned in September 2026 under a 15-ye ar take-or-pay contract, crossing 1,000 TPD installed on-site capacity and promising a full-quarter revenue lift from Q3.

takeaways.label: A ₹480 crore EPC win opens a new strategic door
takeaways.text: The BHEL contract for a 1,200 TPD ASU is lower-margin but zero-balance-sheet-risk work that puts Ellenbarrie in the league to bid for future coal gasification own-and-operate deals.

takeaways.label: Argon mix jumped to 16%, and the story is intact
takeaways.text: Volume from the Uluberia 2 ramp-up and healthy pricing drove the shift; management remains "very constructive" on the long-term demand-supply gap.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: The pace of freight cost normalization, the margin uplift from the Durgapur on-site plant's first full quarter, and any further progress on the north and central India merchant plant timelines.

points.label: Core gases drove the quarter
points.text: The gases business grew ~27% YoY, with the 16% sequential revenue jump reflecting both volume expansion and the initial contribution from the newly commissioned Durgapur on-site plant.

points.label: Durgapur de-risks future revenue
points.text: The 325 TPD plant operates under a 15-year take-or-pay gas supply agreement, meaning fixed monthly revenue with no ramp-up period required, and full-quarter benefit begins Q3 FY27.

points.label: Installed on-site capacity crossed 1,000 TPD
points.text: This milestone matters because customers seeking large-scale supply often require a credential that only industry leaders with plants of this size can show.

points.label: Growth until new merchant plants arrive will come from spare capacity
points.text: Revenue expansion over the next few quarters will be driven by increasing utilization at Uluberia 2 and the new on-site plant, with the north and central India merchant plants expected online only in H2 FY28.

points.label: Long-term revenue ambition stays at 20% annualized growth
points.text: Peak revenue on full utilization of all plants is estimated at ~₹800 crores, with most of the growth coming from volume and a tailwind from greater argon contribution. Management stated the 20% growth guidance applies to the core gases business, not total consolidated revenue.

quotes.text: Padam Kumar Agarwala: "These have been delayed mainly due to the land allotment by the respective state governments and statutory approvals. I think one or two quarters is normal for this size of project, and governments do not work at the speed of industry and business, so whatever we factor in sometimes goes out of hand."

sections.title: Margin Bridge: Noise Above, Strength Below

points.label: Consolidated margin fell on two temporary factors
points.text: EBITDA margin dropped from ~39% in Q1 to ~36% in Q2 because other expenses rose from higher diesel-driven freight costs and longer-distance deliveries, while employee expenses absorbed the payment of annual increment arrears for prior quarters and the buildout of the project engineering team.

points.label: Core gases margin actually improved
points.text: Segment margins for the gases business increased from 38% to 39% QoQ, revealing that the underlying profitability of the main business strengthened even as consolidated optics softened.

points.label: Freight costs carry a 2–3 month pass-through lag
points.text: Diesel-linked transportation costs are contractually pass-through to customers, so the Q2 hit should normalize over the next couple of quarters as the lag catches up.

points.label: Power costs rose with volume, not inefficiency
points.text: Power stayed at ~22% of gas revenue in both Q1 and Q2; absolute gas margins went up, but the EBITDA margin versus revenue was compressed because both cost and revenue rose simultaneously.

points.label: Long-term gas segment margin target is ~40%
points.text: Management is already at 39% and expects the on-site plant's higher-margin revenue contribution in H2 FY27 to meaningfully improve the profile further.

sections.title: The BHEL EPC Contract: A Strategic Credentialing Play

points.label: A ₹480 crore contract with a different risk-return profile
points.text: Awarded by BHEL in late September 2026, the contract covers design, engineering, supply, erection, commissioning and handover of a 1,200 TPD cryogenic air separation unit in Odisha, with execution spread over roughly eight quarters and commissioning expected in FY29.

points.label: This is an EPC contract, not an on-site gas supply deal
points.text: Revenue recognition will follow project progress, with more revenue weighted toward quarters 5–8 than quarters 1–4, and the segment will be clearly bifurcated in reporting.

points.label: Margins are significantly lower by design
points.text: Management characterized the margin profile as "high single digits to low double digits," which is acceptable because the company employs zero long-term capital, only working capital, generating strong absolute cash flow return and high ROCE with no balance sheet risk.

points.label: The real payoff is strategic eligibility
points.text: Executing a 1,000+ TPD plant puts Ellenbarrie into the league of companies qualified to bid for larger projects, crucially opening the door to future long-term own-and-operate contracts for India's emerging coal gasification opportunity, which requires significant oxygen capacity and large ASUs.

quotes.text: Varun Agarwal: "Even though this is an EPC contract, it kind of opens up the room for us to gain long-term contracts where actually we own and operate the asset for other coal gasification projects. So it's very important to put us into the league of companies which are able to execute and which have orders to execute plants with over 1,000 tons per day capacity."

sections.title: Argon: Mix Shift and Pricing Power

points.label: Argon contribution jumped from ~10% to ~16% of revenue QoQ
points.text: Roughly half the increase came from volume as the Uluberia 2 ramp-up produced incremental argon, and half from pricing.

points.label: Long-term demand-supply gap remains constructive
points.text: Demand is increasing faster than supply, prices have stayed healthy around average recent realizations, and management is "very constructive" on argon going forward, expecting the contribution to stay in the mid-teens range of 14–16%.

points.label: Ultra-high-purity gases command a premium
points.text: These are different products from commercial oxygen or argon, requiring extra effort for quality analysis and certification, which must be covered by much higher prices.

points.label: Management declined to disclose quarterly realized prices
points.text: When asked for the specific argon price trend in the past quarter, the company said it does not comment on quarterly realized prices and steered the discussion to long-term trends.

quotes.text: Padam Kumar Agarwala: "It's a different product from commercial oxygen or commercial argon. These are different products, and there is extra effort for quality analysis certification and things like that. So naturally, those extra efforts have to be covered by much higher prices."

points.label: ₹450 crore capex plan for FY27–28 remains on course
points.text: Funding is currently from cash on books, with project-level debt to be taken on as required; nothing is imminent on a capital raise.

points.label: North and central India merchant plants are the next growth leg
points.text: Both plants are expected to come online around the middle of FY28, with revenue contribution starting in H2 FY28 and a ramp-up assumption of 6–8 quarters to full utilization.

points.label: Geographic expansion aims for a balanced pan-India footprint
points.text: Moving toward northern and central India accesses new industrial clusters, diversifies the customer base, and reduces concentration risk.

points.label: Customer capex cycles are moving, just slowly
points.text: Pharma customer conversations are encouraging with many enhancing capacities, which should lead to higher volumes, though in some cases customer capex implementation is taking longer than originally envisaged.

points.label: International expansion is not a near-term priority
points.text: Management sees significant opportunities domestically, noting the company is still at single-digit market share in India, and nothing is imminent on international moves.

items.title: Durgapur on-site plant (Jai Balaji)
items.text: The 325 TPD air separation unit under a 15-year take-or-pay agreement with Jai Balaji Industries was commissioned on 25 September 2026, with revenue starting that month and full-quarter benefit from Q3 FY27. Fixed monthly inflows with no ramp-up lift on-site capacity past 1,000 TPD and should meaningfully improve the margin mix, since on-site plants carry higher EBITDA margins than bulk.

items.title: BHEL coal gasification EPC contract
items.text: A ₹480.73 crore turnkey contract from BHEL, awarded 28 September 2026, covers a 1,200 TPD ASU for the Coal to Ammonium Nitrate project at Jharsuguda - the largest ASU the company has undertaken, with execution over ~24 months and commissioning expected FY29. Larger revenue lands in Quarters 5-8 (from FY28), and at high single-digit to low double-digit margins on working capital alone it adds a cash-generative second stream plus a foothold in India's coal gasification buildout.

items.title: Uluberia 2 ramp-up
items.text: The 220 TPD merchant plant at Uluberia, commissioned in January 2026 with ₹160 crore capex and ~₹100-110 crore revenue potential, is targeting 85% utilisation over 18 months, with management expecting faster ramp given existing customer relationships in the market. Rising utilisation is a named key FY27 growth driver, with argon volumes climbing alongside it.

items.title: Kurnool plant ramp-up (South India)
items.text: The 260 TPD bulk plant at Kurnool is ramping well and, with Uluberia 2, drove the 18% YoY revenue growth in Q1 FY27. It opens Hyderabad and Bengaluru markets, deepening the southern footprint where most of the company's capacity sits.

items.title: Two new merchant plants - North and West/Central India
items.text: ₹450 crore of capex (₹250 crore FY27, ₹200 crore FY28) funds a 220 TPD North India plant and a West/Central India ASU, together ~450-500 TPD, online around mid-FY28 and contributing from H2 FY28. Management sees these taking peak revenue from ~₹400 crore today toward ~₹800 crore at full utilisation, while marking entry into North India and a pan-India footprint.

items.title: Argon mix shift
items.text: Argon and other high-value gases rose to ~16% of the gas mix in Q2 FY27 from ~10% in Q1, roughly half volume and half price, with management guiding a sustained mid-teens contribution on top of ~20% growth. Argon yields significantly higher margins than oxygen and nitrogen, and prices have recovered from the Q3 FY26 lows with further normalisation expected in FY27.

items.title: Renewable power PPAs
items.text: A 25-year wind-solar hybrid PPA with Pattikonda Renewables (6 MW, Ananthapur; ~₹7.08 crore for a minimum 26% stake) was signed on 10 January 2026, covering ~55-60% of one unit's power demand at pricing ~50-60% below grid rates. With power the largest raw material cost at ~22% of gas revenue, benefits start reflecting from FY27, and management is scouting similar PPAs for the other southern plants.
